[QUERENT] classical receptions journal

[SYSTEM]        The Classical Receptions Journal (CRJ) is a peer-reviewed academic journal published by Oxford University Press that focuses on the reception of ancient Greek and Roman texts, ideas, and material culture from antiquity to the present day.
Overview and Scope
• Editor-in-Chief: Justine McConnell (with previous leadership including Pantelis Michelakis).
• Publisher: Oxford University Press.
• ISSN: 1759-5134 (print), 1759-5142 (web).
• Focus: It explores how classical antiquity has been transmitted, translated, adapted, reinterpreted, and reimagined across different historical eras, literature, art, film, and popular culture.
• Cross-Disciplinary: The publication encourages exchange across classics, archaeology, architecture, modern literature, and visual arts.
Related Journals in Classical Reception
• American Journal of Classical Reception (AJCR): Published by Johns Hopkins University Press and sponsored by CAMWS, focusing on the afterlife of classical antiquity in modern media and culture.
• International Journal of the Classical Tradition: Published by Springer, examining the reception of Greco-Roman antiquity from ancient to modern times.
• New Voices in Classical Reception Studies: An open-access journal hosted at The Open University supporting early-career and alternative scholarship.

[QUERENT] what has the journal contributed to study of ai-mediation of the classics?

[SYSTEM] The Classical Receptions Journal has contributed minimally to the direct study of AI-mediation, as the subfield is relatively new and the journal's primary engagement with AI has been through editorial policies rather than dedicated scholarly output.
Current Engagement in the Journal
• Editorial and Authorship Policies: Following Committee on Publication Ethics (COPE) guidelines, the journal formally restricts AI tools from being listed as authors. It requires researchers to disclose any use of generative AI or natural language processing tools—such as for coding, translation, data processing, or image generation—within their cover letters and manuscript acknowledgments.
• Digital Discovery Integration: On the publishing platform side, Oxford Academic hosts an AI Discovery Assistant to help researchers search and surface relevant classical reception scholarship across its archives.
Where AI-Mediation of the Classics is Happening
While CRJ itself has historically focused on traditional literary, theatrical, cinematic, and material receptions, broader conversations around AI-mediation and computational reception are actively emerging in neighboring venues:
• Digital Humanities & Reception: Sister publications like the International Journal of the Classical Tradition have published dedicated special issues (such as Future Pasts: Digital Tools and Classical Reception) examining how generative AI, large language models (LLMs), 3D modeling, and digital archives reshape the transmission and public perception of antiquity.
• Academic Conferences & Workshops: Organizations such as the Classical Reception Studies Network have hosted dedicated events (e.g., Literary Reception and Human Creativity in the Age of AI) exploring how algorithmic text generation compares to human literary adaptation and classical tradition.
• Computational Classics: Adjacent research in machine learning for ancient languages focuses on neural networks restoring damaged epigraphy and papyri, raising critical reception questions regarding algorithmic bias, synthetic text reconstruction, and how machines mediate fragmented historical sources.
